title: Keser as the middle: the Essence's delight in every sefira, Atik and Arich, and Atik Yomin
overview:
Chapter 24 gives the *nimshal* of everything said about will and delight: how it applies to *Keser*. The simple delight of the Essence, *sha'ashuei hamelech b'atzmuso*, is G-d's complete self-expression before the *tzimtzum*, and the ten essential *sefiros* are all part of it; yet the Essence itself is removed even from that and only shines through delight. That desire to reveal Himself comes down through the *ratzon kadum* to the end of everything, like the delight in winning that reaches every move and every t-shirt.

*Atik* and *Arich*, delight and will, are one essence, enclothed in every *sefira* as its existence and encompassing all of them, like oil and like water poured into ten pits. *Atik* still counts as the world of the *Ein Sof*, G-d's free choice; *Arich* is the head of the emanated, so *Keser* is the middle. In detail, *Atik*'s kindness is in the *gulgalta*, so a father at his son's wedding grants anything, and its *gevura* in the hidden wisdom, which is why the Torah has so many exact laws. Above all, *Atik Yomin* is the Essence's eternity shining into time and making it infinite, as a line holds infinite points.

sections.title: The nimshal: everything is from the simple delight, yet the Essence is beyond even delight
sections.summary: The *Keser* of G-d is the *nimshal* of all that was said about will and delight: before the *tzimtzum* there is the simple delight of the Essence, *sha'ashuei hamelech b'atzmuso*, and the ten essential *sefiros* are all its self-expression. Yet the Essence itself is removed even from that; it only shines through delight, which is why nothing in the *hishtalshelus* is higher than pleasure.

איך שבחינת עצמות התענוג הפשוט שבעצמות אור אין סוף קודם הצמצום,
הוא הנקרא שעשועי המלך בעצמותו,
phrases.en: called *sha'ashuei hamelech b'atzmuso*: the *taanug* in Himself,

phrases.he: שהוא בבחינת אין סוף ממש
phrases.en: which is completely unlimited.

phrases.he: וגם בעשר ספירות העצמיים שהוא כתר ועד מלכות דאין סוף, הכל מבחינת העונג הפשוט שבעצמותו
phrases.en: And also the *yud sefiros atzmiyim* are all part of the *taanug pashut sheb'atzmuso*. They're all like a self-expression.

blocks.text: Now he is going to give the *nimshal* (what an analogy stands for) of everything that was said about *ratzon* (will) and *taanug* (delight), and how it applies to *Keser* (crown). Based on what was explained, we can understand how the same thing applies in G-dliness, with what is called the simple *taanug*, the *sha'ashuei hamelech b'atzmuso* (the King's delight in Himself). The real meaning of *taanug* is when something reflects back on the *etzem* (essence).

*Ratzon* is where the *etzem* lowers itself, adapts itself to relate, and invests itself in something that has a particular form. That can be something that is not really outside of it, a part of its own *etzem*, or it can be something outside of it, which is a *ratzon murkav* (a composite will). (He first says *taanug murkav* and corrects himself: "Oh wait, *ratzon murkav*.") And when that thing reflects back on it, that is *taanug*. If the *taanug* comes from something that is a part of its *etzem*, it is a *taanug atzmi* (an essential delight); if it comes from something outside of it, it is a *taanug murkav* (a composite delight).

In the same way, *ratzon* above is G-d's ability to lower Himself, to have something express Him or relate to Him. Either it is a part of the *etzem*, like the ten *sefiros* (the Divine attributes), which is a *mi'ut* (a lessening): to reveal Himself in a limited way. Or it is something outside of His *etzem*: mainly all the particular things of *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya* (the three lower worlds), and even the *kelim* (vessels) of *Atzilus* (the world of Emanation).

The way it is in the *etzem* is called **sha'ashuei hamelech b'atzmuso: the taanug in Himself**, and it is *b'vechinas Ein Sof*, **completely unlimited**. Before the *tzimtzum* (contraction), the *Or Ein Sof* (the infinite light) is the *gilui* (revelation) of G-d in a way that is a complete expression of Him, so the whole *etzem taanug* is there, the whole essential self-expression comes out there, and it is completely infinite. **And also the yud sefiros atzmiyim** (the ten essential *sefiros*) **are all part of the taanug pashut sheb'atzmuso**, the simple delight in His essence. **They're all like a self-expression.**

phrases.he: על דרך משל שגם החסד העצמי שבנפש, עיקר קיומו העונג כו'
phrases.en: just like we see how the main *kiyum* of the *chesed* in a person is the fact that he enjoys it,

blocks.title: Kindness lives on its enjoyment
blocks.text: **Just like we see how the main kiyum** (what keeps it in existence) **of the chesed** (kindness) **in a person is the fact that he enjoys it**, so too the reason G-d limits Himself to all these things is that they are a way to express Himself. There is *taanug* in it.

phrases.he: ועם כל זה באמת הרי עצמות אור אין סוף מובדל גם מבחינת תענוג פשוט
phrases.en: But still the real *Atzmus Or Ein Sof* is removed even from this thing of a *taanug pashut*,

phrases.he: רק שנמשך ומאיר בבחינת העונג,
phrases.en: just that it comes into the *inyan* of pleasure,

phrases.he: כמו שעצמות הנפש תומשך אחר העונג כו'
phrases.en: like the soul is drawn after other things through *taanug*.

blocks.text: **But still the real Atzmus Or Ein Sof** (the Essence of the infinite light) **is removed even from this thing of a taanug pashut**, **just that it comes into the inyan of pleasure**, as the essence of the soul is drawn after pleasure. All of these things are still in the realm of *gilu'im* (revelations).

All of these are revelations, and this is the connection: anything that is able to be a revelation of Him is the way G-d is revealed. **Like the soul is drawn after other things through taanug**, so too the connection between G-d and other things is through what we call *or*, light, which is a revelation of Himself. But we cannot describe the *Atzmus* (G-d's essence) as a *Maor* (the source of light); it is just that it can also do this.

phrases.he: ולזה אמר אין לך למעלה מן העונג כו'
phrases.en: That's why the early *mekubalim* said that there's nothing higher than pleasure.

blocks.text: **That's why the early mekubalim** (Kabbalists) **said that there's nothing higher than pleasure.** That is, there is nothing we can relate to, nothing in the *hishtalshelus* (the chain of descent), that is higher than it. This is the level of the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof*. Above that there is just the *etzem*, which has nothing to do with revelation. So you cannot really call it a level; it is not a thing that goes into the *hishtalshelus*, of which you could say *maala u'mata*, higher and lower.

sections.title: The desire for kindness comes down, through the ratzon kadum, to the end of everything
sections.summary: G-d's *chafetz chesed*, His desire to reveal Himself as a creator, has a simple delight in it, and so it comes down to a separate thing: through the *ratzon kadum* after the *tzimtzum*, the whole *hishtalshelus*, down to the lowest *sefiros* of *Atzilus* that feed the world and run the weather. Like the delight in winning, which reaches every move, the victory dance and all the paraphernalia.

phrases.he: וכמו בבחינת חפץ חסד שבעצמות,
phrases.en: For example, the *inyan* of the *chafetz chesed* in the *Atzmus*: G-d's ability, or His desire, to express Himself,

phrases.he: שיש בו תענוג הפשוט
phrases.en: which has a *taanug pashut*.

phrases.he: הוא נמשך ומאיר בתוספת אור עד שיורד ובא גם בדבר נבדל
phrases.en: So it came down to even come to something *nivdal*,

blocks.text: For example, the *chafetz chesed* (the desire for kindness) in the *Atzmus*: G-d's ability, or His desire, to express Himself, to reveal Himself as a creator. It **has a taanug pashut**: there is a certain unique expression, a revelation of G-d, in it. And just as a person goes after *taanug*, so too with Hashem: this is the reason for the desire to reveal and express this, **so it came down to even come to something nivdal** (separate).

phrases.he: שהוא בבחינת תענוג והרצון הקדום הנזכר לעיל
שאחר הצמצום, להיות מקור להשתלשלות דאבי''ע
phrases.en: to come after *tzimtzum* and to express this thing through actually creating our world, which is the whole *hishtalshelus*

phrases.he: עד שיורד ונמשך בסיום הכל,
phrases.en: until it comes all the way down

phrases.he: והוא גם בפרט דעשר ספירות היותר אחרון שבאצילות
phrases.en: And this is so even of the lowest thing in *Atzilus*, the lowest *sefiros*,

blocks.text: It comes in the form of the *taanug* and the *ratzon kadum* (the primordial will), **to come after tzimtzum and to express this thing through actually creating our world, which is the whole hishtalshelus**, getting more and more until it comes *mamash* (actually) to the world the way we have it now. The *ratzon kadum* is just to create a world that is separate.

**Until it comes all the way down**, to actually create the world as it is now. **And this is so even of the lowest thing in Atzilus, the lowest sefiros**: the level of *Nehi* (*netzach*, *hod* and *yesod*), the way Hashem acts once the world is already seen as something separate and already created, when He gives *mazon* (sustenance) or affects the weather and things like that. Even what creates those things comes from this *taanug pashut*, because there is a unique revelation of G-d in that thing.

phrases.he: על דרך משל הנזכר לעיל בעונג הנמצא לקיום מדת הניצוח וכהאי גוונא
phrases.en: Just like in a person, what keeps up his interest in winning

blocks.title: The victory dance
blocks.text: **Just like in a person, what keeps up his interest in winning** and all the little things that come with it: every little bit he is going to practice, every little move he is going to make to win, and after he wins, the whole victory dance. All these little *pratim* (details) come from the *taanug* he has in *nitzuach* (victory), and so it comes out and is expressed in all these things, until a person gets all into even all the paraphernalia. That is the *orech hadaas* (the length of *daas*). It all comes from the *taanug*, which caused it to spread into this thing.

blocks.title: The fan and the team t-shirt
blocks.text: "Yeah, that's an *orech hadaas*." The fact that people get so into something is called the length of *daas* (knowledge; the mind's bond with what it understands), and it makes them want to have a lot of *asiyos* (deeds), and all the paraphernalia for it. Within that it is a thing of *nitzuach*, but it can also be a thing of wanting to belong, and not *davka* (specifically) sports. There is a special thrill in winning, and by connecting to the team they get the thrill that their team won. They get very connected to it, and since their *daas* is so connected to it, the more they are connected the more they want to know everything about it and have all the paraphernalia, the t-shirt, "and whatever, all the different things."
blocks.outOfPlace: At the end of class 05, after he has read line 14, he comes back to the length of daas in the mashal of line 12, apparently answering a question the recording does not catch.

blocks.title: A fan of G-d
blocks.text: We are soon going to get to chapter one, and there it talks about *daas* in holiness: a person has to become like a fan of G-d. Why would you want to know about all the things in the Torah? This is learning *Torah lishma* (for its own sake): you are learning about things that will never necessarily come up. It is not practical; it is just that you love G-d so much that you want to know everything about Him, what He wants in this thing and that thing. That is why everything of Torah becomes precious, and anything that is *tashmishei kedusha* (an article used for holiness) you want to have very nice, a *hiddur mitzva* (beautifying a commandment): a nice menorah, a nice esrog, all these kinds of things, because you want to express your connection and bring it down into tangible expressions. Everything can be from the side of *kelipa* (lit. husk; what conceals G-dliness) or from the side of *kedusha* (holiness); it can be either.

sections.title: Atik and Arich, delight and will, are one essence: inside every sefira and encompassing them all
sections.summary: *Atik Yomin* and *Arich Anpin* are the delight and the will, one essence, and they are enclothed in every *sefira* down to its smallest detail as its existence. Yet the *Keser* also encompasses them all: like oil it stays above and permeates everything, like water poured into ten pits, like G-d putting on different garments.

phrases.he: וזה שכתוב בעץ חיים, דעתיק יומין ואריך אנפין, שהוא התענוג והרצון, שמהות אחד הם, (ונקרא ג' רישין דמתגלפין דא לגו מן דא כו' ולפעמים זה פנימי
כו' כנזכר לעיל(ואין זה
בלא זה
מלובש תוך כל ספירה וספירה בפרטי פרטות,
phrases.en: the *taanug* and the *ratzon*, which is *Atik* and *Arich*, goes into every single *sefira*, including all of its details, of how they subdivide,

phrases.he: שבלעדו אין לו קיום כלל כנזכר לעיל באריכות
phrases.en: and without it there's no *kiyum* at all,

blocks.text: As it says in *Etz Chaim*, *Atik Yomin* and *Arich Anpin* (lit. the Ancient of Days and the long countenance) are the *taanug* and the *ratzon*, which are one essence, and one is not without the other. ("Let's skip the parentheses for a second.") That is why it says that **the taanug and the ratzon, which is Atik and Arich, goes into every single sefira, including all of its details, of how they subdivide**, how one is enclothed in the other, and all the different combinations that create every single thing.

In every single one there is a unique expression of G-dliness. That is its motivation and its real *kiyum*. And G-d also chose which one to connect Himself to. Just as we said, you can essentially have a *taanug* in something, but if you do not want it, you will not have it. In the same way, even though G-d could express Himself in that thing, He has to want to: He has to lower Himself to choose which way He is going to express Himself, and without that there is no *taanug* in it.

blocks.title: Moral because G-d commanded it?
blocks.text:
Last time he mentioned the old, ancient philosophical question: is morality moral because G-d commanded it, or did He command it because it is moral? This is exactly the question of which comes first, *Atik* or *Arich*. And the answer is that they are really synonymous, so you can never say which one comes first; if you look into the *etzem*, it is really one thing.

There is a unique *taanug* in the thing of morality, but if G-d had not chosen that thing, He could also have chosen to have the unique *taanug* that is in something else. From that side, G-d's *ratzon* comes first. On the other hand, the reason G-d chose it is that it was the unique thing He wanted: He wanted to reveal that thing, so there is something unique about it, which is what He chose. So it is a *bechira* (choice), and what makes it good is the choice; and on the other hand Hashem wanted that it should be *davka* because of its virtues.
So these are enclothed in everything, **and without it there's no kiyum at all**, as explained above at length.

phrases.he: וגם הוא מקיף את כולם
phrases.en: but on the other hand, it's also *makif* all of them.

blocks.text: **But on the other hand, it's also makif** (encompassing) **all of them.** On the one hand, there is a unique *taanug* and *ratzon* for each thing, which is what makes that thing. But on the other hand, the *etzem taanug* and *ratzon* is really higher than all of them; it is just for Himself, and it does not really matter to it whether it is this way or that way.

But once it chooses, it gets connected to one form, as was learned in *Tarsach* (5668). Once we are speaking of the real *ratzon*, which is to be happy, a person connects that to a *ratzon* for money and food and *kavod* (honor) and all these things. Then there is a unique *taanug* and *ratzon* for each thing, and a person can become very connected to one of them. But those are only the *middos* (attributes) of the *ratzon*. The real *etzem ratzon* and *taanug* is just that he is expressing himself, feeling his vitality. That is really higher than all of them; to it, it is all the same, and it could pick something else. Just once it picks something, it puts itself into it.

blocks.title: Choosing one path in life
blocks.text: It is like having to choose what path you are going to take in life, what you are going to specialize in. From the side of your *etzem* you could do anything, but if you want to actually do anything, *b'poel mamash*, you have to pick one thing to do.

blocks.title: Oil stays apart and permeates
blocks.text: So the same way, the *Keser* is *makif* all the *sefiros*. The real *etzem* of all the *sefiros* is the same thing, and it is really higher than any of them; it is just a revelation of G-d. And therefore it is *mefa'pe'a*, it spreads into everything, like oil: oil stays separate from everything, and it spreads into everything. "This does not mix with anything, and this permeates everything." That is the *Keser*: the *etzem* that is higher than everything, and yet also spreads into everything individually.

This is what it says, that *Chassidus* (Chassidic teaching) is a new revelation of *Keser*, of a new light from *Keser*, really the *ra'ava d'chol ra'avin* (the will of all wills). Because the point of *Chassidus* is to reveal this *etzem* of everything, how everything is meant to be, and really is, a revelation of G-d. That is why in *Kuntres Inyana shel Toras HaChassidus* he explains these two things, that it is higher than everything and that it comes into everything, and compares it to oil. This is all the matter of *Keser*.

phrases.he: )וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר במשל עשר חפירות זה אחר זה שהראשונה נמשכת בתוך כל חפירה וחפירה כו'
phrases.en: like it's explained elsewhere about a *mashal* of ten pits, one after the other, like an ice cube tray: if you pour water into the first one, it will fill it up, and then it will overflow into the second, then into the third, and then it will fill them all up.

phrases.he: וכך אמר בזהר עבד מנא רברבא וקארי בה גרמיה חכים כו'
phrases.en: Hashem made many garments, and He called them wisdom and understanding,

phrases.he: וכן מה שכתוב אפיק עשר תיקונין וקרינן לון עשר ספירות כו׳)
phrases.en: Hashem made ten garments, *tikunin* means garments, and He called them ten *sefiros*.

blocks.title: Ten pits, like an ice cube tray
blocks.text: **Like it's explained elsewhere about a mashal of ten pits, one after the other, like an ice cube tray: if you pour water into the first one, it will fill it up, and then it will overflow into the second, then into the third**, until it fills them all up. This is how it works: "I think" the water is like the *Keser*, the *ratzon* and *taanug*. It first pours into *chachma* (wisdom), then it automatically overflows into *bina* (understanding), and so it overflows into all of them.

blocks.title: Water takes the shape of the vessel
blocks.text: So it goes into each one individually and fits it, the way water takes the shape of the *kli* (vessel). But the water is really the same in all of them, and it is not really limited to any *kli*. If each one had a different color, it would look different, and they give all these different *meshalim* (analogies); but the *etzem or* is really the same thing.

And this is what it says in the *Zohar*: **Hashem made many garments, and He called them wisdom and understanding.** The ten *sefiros* are just like *levushim* (garments). The *etzem* is really the same in each one, and its external form is different according to the *kli*. The *etzem* of all of them is the same, and it is really G-d, just putting on different garments.

blocks.title: A sage at Sinai, a warrior at the Sea
blocks.text: First He dresses up and acts out the role of a wise person: as it says, at *Matan Torah* (the giving of the Torah) they saw Him as a sage with a long white beard, and at *Krias Yam Suf* (the splitting of the Sea) they saw Him as a young warrior. One time He put on the clothes of *netzach* (victory), and the other time the clothes of *chachma*, but it is the same *Aibershter* (the One Above).
And what it says, "He brought out ten *tikunin* and called them ten *sefiros*", means the same thing: **Hashem made ten garments, tikunin means garments, and He called them ten sefiros.**

sections.title: Keser as the middle: Atik is still the world of the Infinite, Arich is the head of what is emanated
sections.summary: *Atik Yomin* still counts as the end of the world of the *Ein Sof*, because everything down to *Malchus* of *Adam Kadmon* is still G-d's free choice, like a drawing of a tree that is still infinite. *Arich Anpin*, the will that comes from the delight to make a world, is already the head of the emanated. So *Keser* is the *memutza*: the end of the Essence and the head of the *ne'etzalim*, which are separate from the Essence the way a kind man's coats are separate from his kindness.

phrases.he: להיות כי בחינת עתיק יומין נחשב מסוף עולם האין סוף עדיין
phrases.en: that *Atik* is considered the end of the *Ein Sof* still.

phrases.he: לפי שעולם האין סוף נחשב עד בחינת מלכות דאדם קדמון, שהוא בחינת אותיות וסוף מעשה שעלה במחשבה ורצון הקדום הנזכר לעיל

blocks.text: Because **Atik is considered the end of the Ein Sof still.** The *olam ha'Ein Sof* (the world of the Infinite) is counted until *Malchus* of *Adam Kadmon* (lit. primordial man; the first world). What does it mean that it is still unlimited? It means that it is still a free *bechira* (choice). So the *Kav* (the ray of light) is still called like *bechira*: sometimes the world of the *Ein Sof* is counted until *Malchus* of *Adam Kadmon*, sometimes all the way down to *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, and sometimes even the way it is enclothed in the *kelim* of *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya* is called the world of the *Ein Sof*. Because even if I give you just two choices, it is still an expression of your *bechira*.

blocks.title: Draw me a tree
blocks.text: Or even more than that: if I say, "Okay, I'm going to give you a pen and a paper, and I want you to make me a picture of a tree," I gave you very severe limitations, but the possibilities are still infinite, because you can still express yourself however you want. So even though G-d already chose to reveal Himself in a limited way, through *Adam Kadmon*, only through the ten *sefiros*, the way He can use them is still infinite. Therefore it is still considered the world of the *Ein Sof*, and sometimes even what comes after it is considered the world of the *Ein Sof*.

phrases.he: והוא בחינת אחרונה שבעצמות שנעשה כתר דעתיק יומין,
שזהו בחינת גלוי אור העונג מהעלם העונג ורצון קדום הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: This is the *gilui* of the *etzem taanug*, which was in the *ratzon kadum*,

phrases.he: על כן גם כתר דעתיק יומין וחכמה ובינה ומדות שבו, הכל נחשב מסוף עולם האין סוף
phrases.en: Therefore *Atik* is still considered the end of the world of *Ein Sof*.

blocks.text:
It is the last level of the Essence, which becomes the *Keser* of *Atik Yomin*. Since Hashem chose that He is going to reveal Himself through this external form, which is in the *Malchus* of *Adam Kadmon*, that is still His choice. So it is *Ein Sof*, because nothing was imposed on Him; He chose it. And therefore the *taanug* He gets, the revelation of Himself that comes out through this, is still a direct revelation of His *etzem*, because this is His *bechira*: He put His *etzem* into it, *mamash*.

**This is the gilui of the etzem taanug, which was in the ratzon kadum**, that He wanted to reveal Himself through creating a world, and this is the form He decided to reveal Himself as, or through. **Therefore Atik is still considered the end of the world of Ein Sof**, with its *Keser*, *chachma*, *bina* and *middos*.

phrases.he: אבל בחינת אריך אנפין שהוא בחינת גלוי הרצון שבא מחמת העונג להיותו נמשך ובא להתפשט למטה כו', הוא הנקרא ראש ושרש הנאצלים, שהן עשר ספירות דאצילות בכלל ובפרט

blocks.text: But *Arich Anpin*, the revelation of the will that comes because of the delight, to be drawn down and spread below, is called the head and root of the *ne'etzalim* (what is emanated). That is the *ratzon* that comes out from this: since Hashem wants to reveal Himself in this way, therefore He is going to want to create a world like this and do such and such. That is already considered something outside relative to this. It is already not the *etzem taanug*, not the *etzem* thing; it is just the means to the end. These are the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus*, in general and in detail.

phrases.he: ולזה נקרא בחינת הכתר בכלל בחינת ממוצע,
phrases.en: This is why *Keser* in general is called a *memutza*,

phrases.he: שיש בו מבחינת אחרונה שבעצמות, והוא ראש לנאצלים
phrases.en: It has both the end of the *Atzmus*, and it's also the beginning of the *ne'etzalim*.

blocks.text: **This is why Keser in general is called a memutza** (a middle). **It has both the end of the Atzmus, and it's also the beginning of the ne'etzalim.**

phrases.he: כי אורות הנאצלים שהן בחינת גילוי ההעלם, הרי הן בבחינת נבדל מן העצמות כנזכר לעיל (באות י''ב) וכמו על דרך משל המדות חסד וגבורה בדבר נבדל, שבאין מכח המדות חסד וגבורה שבעצם כו'

blocks.title: The nice guy's coats
blocks.text: The lights of the *ne'etzalim*, which are a *gilui ha'helem* (revelation of what is hidden), are separate from the Essence, as said above. (He adds: "The *os* is supposed to be a *tes*.") As we said: the essential choice of a person that he wants to be a nice guy comes from his *etzem*. But that in such and such a circumstance, in such a society, being kind is connected to giving people *tzedaka* (charity), or helping people, giving them coats or shoes or any kind of nice thing, is circumstantial; it is not really from his choice. So in a way you could say that, in general, that is already something separate.

On the other hand, sometimes it says that even the end of *Atzilus* is part of the *Ein Sof*, because even within these things there are still choices of exactly how to do it and how much to express each of the different *middos*.

As with the attributes of *chesed* and *gevura* (might, restraint) in a separate thing, which come from the power of the *chesed* and *gevura* in the essence. A person who actually has a *ratzon* for a certain thing is just expressing his *etzem chesed*, his essential *ratzon* for *chesed* or for *gevura*. But that thing is not really an expression of the *etzem*. The fact that a person chooses to be nice is his self-expression; the particular thing he did depends, and from what comes out of it you could get the wrong idea. You are not necessarily going to see the *etzem* in it unless you understand how it is connected, what he means by it.

blocks.title: Masked men at the table
blocks.text: As the Rebbe likes to bring down: if you see a bunch of people strapping somebody down to a table and masked men cutting him up, you would think they are terrible, horrible people torturing this poor guy, and really they are surgeons trying to save his life. So the revelation that comes out from that is already something separate. Unless you know how to connect it back to what they mean to express, you are not going to see the revelation of the *etzem* there. But once you do see it, the revelation comes all the way down.

That is really the main point of going through the *shorashim* (roots): to keep seeing it. Once you understand the language, how these levels connect, you see how the *etzem or* comes over to the next level, and the next level.

sections.title: The delight enclothed in everything is its existence; without it, a thing is neglected
sections.summary: The delight and will that come from the Essence are enclothed in everything, as what keeps it in existence every moment, because G-d wants to reveal Himself through it. Delight means the soul is expressed through a thing; so *kelipa*, which opposes it, has no real existence, and even a king would drop his kingship if he took no pleasure in it.

phrases.he: ועם כל זה בחינת התענוג והרצון שבא מן העצמות, הוא מלובש תוך כל, להיות קיומם תמיד כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: But nevertheless, this *taanug* and *ratzon* that comes from the *etzem* goes into every single little thing that he's choosing what he wants to do.

phrases.he: מפני ששרש זה התענוג והרצון, בעצמות אור אין סוף שנקרא שעשועי המלך בעצמו כו'

blocks.text: **But nevertheless, this taanug and ratzon that comes from the etzem goes into every single little thing that he's choosing what he wants to do.** So everything is a revelation of his *etzem*: what motivates that attribute is that he wants to express himself as that kind of person.

Because the root of this *taanug* and *ratzon* is in the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof*, which is called the *sha'ashuei hamelech b'atzmo*. Now we are already talking about the *nimshal*: the reason the world is the way it is, and G-d in every single thing that happens, is that Hashem wants to reveal that aspect of His *etzem*; He wants to reveal Himself through that thing. If we learn to see it, we will understand what He is really revealing. Sometimes we can get the wrong idea and not appreciate what He is trying to reveal.

phrases.he: וכמשל הנפש שנמשך אחר כל עונג כו',
phrases.en: Like the soul that goes after every pleasure,

phrases.he: שמזה ראיה שהעונג ממלא אורה כו'
phrases.en: From this we see that the *taanug* fills up the light of the soul,

phrases.he: אם כן גם מזה עצמו הוא הטעם שהעונג פרטי שבכל פרט מן האורות, הוא עיקר קיומו כו'
phrases.en: That's why the *taanug* in each thing, that is really the *etzem* of that thing,

blocks.text: **Like the soul that goes after every pleasure. From this we see that the taanug fills up the light of the soul**: it is like a revelation of the *etzem*, which expresses itself through this thing. That is what *taanug* means: the soul is being expressed through that thing. And therefore the more *taanug* it gets in something, the more it connects to it, because it expresses more of itself through this thing.

**That's why the taanug in each thing, that is really the etzem of that thing**: that is what the soul gets out of it. You say, "Well, what do I get out of it? Why do I want to do it?" The same thing above: what keeps everything existing every single moment is that G-d has a *taanug* in it, meaning that the thing is somehow revealing G-dliness. That is why *kelipa* is called a nonentity, like a shadow, with no real *metzius* (existence): the whole existence of things is G-d's *ratzon* and *taanug* in them, and something that is the opposite does not really have existence.

blocks.question: If the existence of everything is G-d's delight in it, what about people who feel a delight in what is bad?
blocks.text: "They're feeling a *taanug*, but the question is what are they feeling a *taanug* from?" It depends. Sometimes they are feeling a good *taanug* in G-dliness, but they are messing it up, taking it out of context. They take one little thing and disconnect it from the real point, as if you would take the guy's kindness and separate it from his *etzem*; then it becomes a bad thing. The excitement they feel is really good, just that they are being sold something false: they are told that this is connected, that this is true, that if you do this and this, let's say, you will win. So they are all excited, anticipating that they will be able to be like that, and then it is not true. Their real *ratzon*, the real *taanug* they are looking for, is not bad; just the way it comes out is bad.

phrases.he: עד גם בבחינת המלכות שהוא ההתנשאות
phrases.en: Even, same thing, even with *Malchus*, to be a king,

phrases.he: לולי התענוג שבו אין לו קיום כו'
phrases.en: if there wouldn't be a *taanug* in being king, you wouldn't want to do it.

phrases.he: והעדר אור העונג הוא בחינת העדר אור מציאותם כו'
phrases.en: But now if you'll have a want of pleasure in it, then he'll neglect it and pull away from it

phrases.he: ודי למבין.
וכל זה דרך כלל
phrases.en: But that's only in general.

blocks.text: The same thing **even with Malchus** (kingship), **to be a king: if there wouldn't be a taanug in being king, you wouldn't want to do it.** **But now if you'll have a want of pleasure in it, then he'll neglect it and pull away from it** and get involved in other things. This is the general matter of how *Atik* and *Arich* relate to each other and to the *sefiros* and everything. **But that's only in general**, and now he is going to say a little more detail.

sections.title: In detail: only the three heads of Atik count as the Essence; its kindness opens the will
sections.summary: In detail, only the three heads of *Atik* belong to the Essence; its seven lower attributes are enclothed in *Arich*, its kindness in the *gulgalta* and its *gevura* in the *mocha stima'a*. The will is born from the attributes of the delight: a father at his son's wedding, flooded with delight, will grant anything and turn even judgment into kindness, because it reaches the point of will above the hidden reason.

phrases.he: אבל דרך פרט, הנה רק בחינת ג׳ ראשין דעתיק יומין נחשב מבחינת העצמות
phrases.en: In particular, only the *Keser*, *chachma*, *bina* of *Atik* is considered part of the *etzem*,

phrases.he: אבל ז׳ תחתונים שבו מלובש בגלגלתא דאריך אנפין
phrases.en: but the seven *middos* of *Atik* are enclothed into *Arich* already.

phrases.he: חסד דעתיק יומין בגלגלתא
phrases.en: The *chesed* of *Atik* goes into the skull, the *Keser* of *Arich*,

phrases.he: וגבורה במוחא סתימאה כו'
phrases.en: and *gevura* goes into the *mocha stima'a*, the *chachma* of *Arich*,

blocks.text: **In particular, only the Keser, chachma, bina of Atik is considered part of the etzem**, the *gimmel reishin* (the three heads); that is like the *Reisha d'lo isyada* (the head that is not known). **But the seven middos of Atik are enclothed into Arich already.**

The way it goes: **the chesed of Atik goes into the skull, the Keser of Arich, and gevura goes into the mocha stima'a** (the hidden brain), **the chachma of Arich**, and *tiferes* (beauty) of *Atik* goes into *bina* of *Arich*. Then *netzach*: generally it goes straight down, but really the inner side of *netzach* and *hod* and the outer side get split up. "Forget exactly the order." These are called the seven *tikunim* of the *gulgalta* (the skull), and they correspond to *chesed* through *Malchus* of *Atik*. Then there are the thirteen *tikunim* of the *dikna* (the beard), which are the *tikunim* of *Arich*. So these are the *tikunim* of *Atik*, and then there are the *tikunim* of *Arich*, and he will explain it a little.

phrases.he: כידוע, להיות כי התהוות עיקר הרצון מן התענוג, הוא רק מבחינת המדות שבתענוג
phrases.en: The *ratzon* comes *davka* from the *middos* of the *taanug*.

phrases.he: כמו מן החסד שבתענוג

blocks.text: As is known, the coming into being of the will from the delight is only from the attributes in the delight: **the ratzon comes davka from the middos of the taanug.** The *ratzon* is really a means to the end: since you want to get a *taanug* in such and such a form, you are going to need such and such a *ratzon*. For example, from the *chesed* in the *taanug*.

phrases.he: על דרך משל, כאשר אדם בעונג בשמחת חתונת בנו וכהאי גוונא,
phrases.en: Like for example if a person's at a wedding, at their son's wedding,

phrases.he: אז יטיב רב חסדו לכל
מצד התענוג שמרומם את נפשו
phrases.en: because they get such a big *taanug*,

phrases.he: (מטעם הנזכר לעיל)

blocks.title: At his son's wedding
blocks.text: **Like for example if a person's at a wedding, at their son's wedding**: **because they get such a big taanug**, you will be able to get them to say yes to anything. They are feeling the *chesed* of *taanug*: the *chesed* of *taanug* is a big felt pleasure, and the *gevura* of *taanug* is like pain. The fact that they have a big felt pleasure creates the *etzem ratzon*: they just want to express themselves, they want to let everybody know, let the world know, so they want to do just anything; they do not really care what it is.

phrases.he: ואז יפעלו ממנו כל רצון
phrases.en: then you can get them to want anything,

phrases.he: דהיינו להפוך גם מרצון של דין לחסד
phrases.en: So even if he was before angry at somebody or whatever, you can turn it over,

phrases.he: שזה תלוי בבחינת נקודת הרצון שלמעלה מטעם כמוס לרצון,
phrases.en: this is connecting to *etzem ratzon*, the *nekuda* which is higher than the reason for *ratzon*.

phrases.he: שמחלק לחסד וגבורה, חסד ודין כו'

blocks.text: **Then you can get them to want anything**, even to turn a will of judgment into kindness: **so even if he was before angry at somebody or whatever, you can turn it over**, or like kings would a lot of times pardon people at the wedding of their son.

Because **this is connecting to etzem ratzon, the nekuda** (point) **which is higher than the reason for ratzon.** The *ta'am kamus* (the hidden reason) of the will means that you want a *taanug davka* in a certain way: you want things only if they fit a certain form. But this is the *etzem* thing: he does not really care whether it is this *taanug* or that; he just wants anything that will express himself, because he feels such a big *hispashtus* (spreading forth) of his existence that he needs *kelim* to fill it, and he does not care which *kelim*; it can fit in anything. Normally he limits himself and picks only certain ones, the reason that divides into *chesed* and *gevura*, *chesed* and *din* (judgement). Once he is in the *ta'am kamus*, it already becomes a *ratzon murkav*: there are certain things he wants and certain things he does not. But here it is an essential thing.

As it talks about in *Yafa Sha'ah Achas* about the head: when a *taanug* comes through so much, it goes over the whole head, it goes to everything, so it does not really matter; he wants everything. Normally it only comes in a very little bit, it drips down, and so he only wants certain things that are easy to get *taanug* from, according to his *kelim*.

phrases.he: וזהו דוגמא להבין איך שבחינת חסד דעתיק יומין מלובש בגלגלתא כו'
phrases.en: This is the way that the *chesed* of *Atik* is *meluvash* in the *gulgalta*,

blocks.text: And this is the likeness by which to understand how **the chesed of Atik is meluvash** (enclothed) **in the gulgalta**: in other words, it goes into this liquid: that is the *chesed* of *Atik*.

sections.title: Gevura in the hidden wisdom: why chachma is judgment, and why the Torah has many laws
sections.summary: The *gevura* of *Atik*, judgment and the opposite of delight, is enclothed in the *mocha stima'a*, the hidden reason of the will: the delight only drips through in certain places, so the will is exacting, this way and not another. That is why the early Kabbalists said *chachma* is judgment, and why the Torah, from the higher wisdom, has so many exact laws.

phrases.he: ובחינת גבורה, שהוא בחינת הדין, בהיפך לעונג,
phrases.en: The *gevura*, which is the *din*, which means from pain, the opposite of the *oneg*,

phrases.he: הוא מלובש בחכמה סתימאה דאריך אנפין, שהוא טעם כמוס לרצון
שזהו לדקדק ברצון, שיהיה באופן זה דוקא ולא באופן אחר כו'

blocks.text: The skull is from the *chesed* of *Atik*, and this liquid is the *mocha stima'a*, and the skull forces it down into really everywhere in the head. Then the *kruma* (the membrane) is from *tiferes* of *Atik*, which makes it come out in some places more and in some places less: that is the *bina* of *Arich*, which associates the *taanug* with certain things. The *gevura*, though, means that it comes only a little bit through the hairs, it drips through only a little; that is the *mocha stima'a* of *Arich Anpin*, which is the *ta'am kamus* of the will, and it comes to the thing of pain.

("Wait, did I skip this?" He goes back and reads the line.) **The gevura, which is the din, which means from pain, the opposite of the oneg** (delight), is enclothed in the *mocha stima'a* of *Arich Anpin*, which makes a *ta'am kamus*: to be exacting in the will, that it should be *davka* this way and not another. Since it drips only in very limited places and in a very limited way, he is only going to get *taanug* in a certain form and in certain places, not everywhere. And so he wants only certain things; it gives his *ratzon* a certain direction.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב בספרי הקבלה שהראשונים גזרו אומר על החכמה שהיא בבחינת דין
phrases.en: That's why they said the *chachma* is on the side of *din*,

phrases.he: שכאשר הרצון בא על פי חיוב החכמה, בא בדקדוק וצמצום, כך ולא כך

blocks.text: As it says in the books of Kabbala, the early ones declared that *chachma* is *din*. **That's why they said the chachma is on the side of din**: because it limits the *ratzon* to come out in a certain form, *davka*. When the will comes by the necessity of *chachma*, it comes exactingly and limited, this way and not that way. Since he gets pain from certain things, it becomes nitpicky: he wants to avoid the things that are painful, he has to go around them, and he involves himself only with things that are pleasurable.

phrases.he: ועל כן על פי משפט התורה, דאורייתא מחכמה עילאה כו',
phrases.en: and this is why the Torah, which comes from *chachma ila'a*,

phrases.he: יש דינים רבים
phrases.en: There's a lot of *dinim*.

blocks.text: **And this is why the Torah, which comes from chachma ila'a** (the higher wisdom), has many laws: **there's a lot of dinim.** Most of the *mitzvos* (commandments) are *lo sa'aseh*, do nots, and even the *asei*'s are very exacting; it has to be *davka* this way. *Tefillin* has to be exactly right to be kosher, or else it is nothing.

sections.title: Above wisdom: the thirteen attributes of mercy, the source of all delights, and the eternity of Atik Yomin
sections.summary: Above wisdom, the thirteen attributes of mercy are the essential delight in the *gulgalta*, which can take delight in anything and forgives sin; and the three heads of *Atik* are the delight as it is in itself, before any will, the source of all delights. *Atik Yomin* means the eternity of the Essence as it shines into time: higher than time, it makes time infinite, as a line holds infinite points.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן הארת י''ג מדות הרחמים מלמעלה מחכמה שברצון כו',
שנושא עון וכו'
phrases.en: that He forgives sin.

blocks.text: But the light of the thirteen *middos harachamim* (attributes of mercy), from above the *chachma* that is in the will, is the *etzem taanug* in the *gulgalta*. There Hashem could really get *taanug* from anything; it does not have to be *davka* according to the Torah. There is really a revelation of G-d also in an *aveira* (a sin): the fact that we are connected is really expressed, and in an *aveira* it is just expressed in a negative way. And so, **that He forgives sin.**

phrases.he: ומכל שכן מבחינת ג׳ ראשין דעתיק יומין שבלתי מלובש בנאצלים
phrases.en: and how much more so when we connect to the *gimmel reishin* of *Atik Yomin*, that it's not at all clothed in *ne'etzalim*,

phrases.he: והוא בחינת העונג כמו שהוא בעצמו
שעדיין לא נולד ממנו רצון כלל,
phrases.en: This is just the *etzem taanug* before it's related to anything outside, which makes a *ratzon*.

phrases.he: רק עתיד להיות ממנו כל רצון כו'
phrases.en: which is the *makor* which causes every *ratzon*.

blocks.text: **And how much more so when we connect to the gimmel reishin of Atik Yomin, that it's not at all clothed in ne'etzalim.** There it is just the essential connection to the Yidden, totally beyond anything we do or do not do. It is the delight as it is in itself, from which no will has been born at all: **this is just the etzem taanug before it's related to anything outside, which makes a ratzon**, only that the power of will is to come from it, **which is the makor** (source) **which causes every ratzon.** That is like the *yechida* (the essence of the soul) of a Jew, the way it is connected to G-d in essence.

phrases.he: והוא נחשב מעצמות התענוג הפשוט הכללי
שהוא מבחינת מקור כל התענוגים שבעצמות אור אין סוף
כמו שכתוב כי עמך מקור חיים,
phrases.en: "With You is the source of life,"

phrases.he: מקור כל התענוגים שברצון קדום כו'
phrases.en: this is the source of everything that comes in the *ratzon kadum*,

phrases.he: ונקרא עתיקא דעתיקין בכללות הכל כו'
phrases.en: it's called *Atik* of all *Atik*'s,

blocks.text: It counts as the essence of the simple, general delight, the source of all the delights in the *Atzmus Ein Sof*. In a person, it is like the soul before it comes in at all. As it says, **"With You is the source of life"**: the source of all the delights in the *ratzon kadum*; **this is the source of everything that comes in the ratzon kadum.** And it is called *Atika d'Atikin*: **it's called Atik of all Atik's**, and all of it hidden.

phrases.he: ונקרא עתיק יומין כמו שכתוב בדניאל, ועתיק יומין יתיב כו',
phrases.en: And in general, pleasure is called *Atik Yomin*... "The Ancient of Days sat."

phrases.he: מלשון זקנה
phrases.en: means old age,

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת נצחיות דעצמיות אור אין סוף
כשבא ומאיר למטה בהשתלשלות דקו וחוט כו'
phrases.en: when it comes into time, it becomes infinite.

blocks.text: **In general, pleasure is called Atik Yomin**, as it says in Daniel, **"The Ancient of Days sat."** *Mi'lashon zikna*: it **means old age**, which is the eternity of the *Atzmus Ein Sof*. The *Atzmus Ein Sof* is beyond changing, and change is time. Being totally beyond all forms and change means that it can come into anything, and so, no matter what changes, it will still be there. That is what it means that the *etzem* is eternal. It is really higher than time, but **when it comes into time, it becomes infinite.**

phrases.he: אבל בעצמותו ממש, מי איכא זקנה קמי קודשא בריך הוא כו'
phrases.en: is there any age? How can you say that He's old?

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין ועד בחלופי אתוון דאחד
phrases.en: That *va'ed*, forever, eternal, is like a *chiluf* of *echad*,

phrases.he: פשוט עצמו

blocks.text: But in His Essence itself, before the Holy One, blessed be He, **is there any age? How can you say that He's old?** Because it's above time. As is explained elsewhere, *va'ed* is an exchange of the letters of *echad*: **that va'ed, forever, eternal, is like a chiluf** (an exchange) **of echad**. Since Hashem's unity is totally unified and beyond any type of division, the *etzem* is higher than everything; therefore it can come into anything, no changes in time can affect it, and so it is infinite.

phrases.he: שעצמות אור אין סוף שלמעלה מן הזמן דימי קדם כו',
כשמאיר בזמן, אז הזמן גם כן נצחי
phrases.en: So then the time itself becomes infinite.

phrases.he: כו' ואז נקרא עתיק יומין
phrases.en: then it's called *Atik Yomin*,

phrases.he: כו' ודי למבין:

blocks.text: The *Atzmus Ein Sof*, which is above time, when it shines into time, then time too is eternal: **so then the time itself becomes infinite.** Normally it is impossible to have something made up of finite parts go on forever, and time is made up of finite parts, seconds and hours and days and years.

blocks.title: Cheerios in a row
blocks.text: Let's say you take a bunch of Cheerios and start putting them next to each other, and you keep adding. You will never get to an infinity, because no matter how big a number you get, since you are starting with finite parts, relative to an infinity they are all like zeros, and if you add zeros you never get anywhere. So it is impossible, starting from a finite power, to build something up until it is infinite.

blocks.title: Points and a line
blocks.text: But take something like geometry. Points have no space; they are zero-dimensional. If you take a bunch of points and start putting them next to each other, you will never get a line, or even a line segment; you will never get any length, because they are all infinitely small. They are zeros. But if you take a line, that line automatically holds infinite points: that is how they define a line, an infinite series of points. Because it is really something higher than the whole matter of points, and therefore when it comes in, it makes it infinite.

blocks.title: Can time be infinite?
blocks.text: In the same way, it is really impossible to have time be infinite. People talk about it in *chakira* (philosophical inquiry), and the *Tzemach Tzedek* talks about it a little. It is not really true; really you can have infinite time. The Rebbe talks about it in a *sicha* (a talk), but it is like a *mah nafshach* (an either-way argument). If you talk from human intellect, starting with the limitations of the world, it is impossible to have infinite time, and therefore there must have been a certain time when the world started, when it was created: that is the proof. And if you say that it is infinite, then you must admit that it comes from a miraculous higher reality that is able to give our reality an infinite being, and then again you must admit that there is a G-d that made it. That is the point there; but here he is saying the actual reality: it comes into time, and therefore makes it eternal.

And then **it's called Atik Yomin**, from the word for old age, when it comes in, because the *middos* of *Atik* are called *Atik Yomin*. The *etzem* of *Atik* is just called plain *Atik*: it is totally removed from anything; it is not that it is infinite time, infinite *yomin* (days); it is just separate. *Atik Yomin* is the way it already relates to *Beriya*, to creation: Hashem already gets a *taanug*, there is already G-dliness within creation, and then it makes the creation itself G-dly and infinite. And this is enough for one who understands.

reviewQuestions.question: If the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof* is removed even from the simple delight, why did the early Kabbalists say that nothing is higher than pleasure?
What does the delight in winning, down to the victory dance and the paraphernalia, show about the *taanug pashut*, and what does it mean to be a fan of G-d?
How can the *Keser* be enclothed in every *sefira* and also encompass them all? What do the oil, the ten pits and the garments show?
Why is *Atik Yomin* still counted as the end of the world of the *Ein Sof*, and what does the drawing of a tree have to do with it?
Why will a father at his son's wedding grant anything, even turn judgment into kindness, and what level of the will does that reach?
Why did the early Kabbalists call *chachma* judgment, and how does that explain the many exact laws of the Torah?
